clips.send: Someone who lives for the city sends this to a friend glued to their desk, proof that a walk somewhere loud with crickets is doing more for their brain than a quiet office ever will.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the wealthy did not stumble onto this by accident: the most powerful nature sounds - crickets, cicadas, frogs, birds - are the repeated ones, and that repetition stimulates the hippocampus, the part of the brain tied to manifesting goals.

Step into a forest and there is a second mechanism. Wind moving through the trees produces negative ions, and those ions stimulate the hippocampus and the pineal gland even further.

None of it costs a membership. A loud patch of crickets or a beach with rolling waves does the same thing, he says.

When did you last let a forest fill your ears instead of a podcast?
